topic: Provider account action feedback without layout shift
stack_version_constraints: Use the existing workspace-monitor renderer stack.
Do not add a new UI dependency or native command for this narrow feedback change.

language_options.fit: Best fit because the feedback is renderer state tied to existing provider buttons.
Not selected because native command behavior does not need to change.

language_decision_notes: Provider errors are already produced by renderer command handlers; TypeScript state and CSS can express the UI contract without changing Rust storage or command APIs.

architecture_options.reason: Too broad and would not directly tie the error to the button the user pressed.
Smallest scoped change; it keeps the error on the relevant button and avoids inserting visible layout text.

architecture_practitioner_sources: Existing provider settings panel and renderer tests
architecture_decision_notes: Button-local state plus a hidden live region satisfies visual stability and accessibility without broad UI migration.
architecture_tradeoff_notes: A small badge is less verbose than a paragraph, so the full message is exposed through title and aria-label.
The pattern is currently scoped to provider settings; global error design can be handled later.

folder_structure_options.option: Create a new feedback component folder
folder_structure_options.reason: The behavior is narrow and local to ProviderAccountsPanel.
Avoids abstraction before reuse and keeps the change easy to audit.

folder_structure_decision_notes: No source folder was created; only scoped renderer, CSS, tests, and project/history artifacts changed.
folder_semantics_notes: Provider action feedback remains part of the provider accounts settings surface.
maintainability_notes: Readiness tokens prevent removing the local feedback contract silently.
Renderer tests check that visible provider error paragraphs do not return.
code_reference_notes: Existing provider credential handlers were reused.
CSS reserves badge space from the initial render to prevent size shifts.
issue_discussion_notes: No high-signal issue/discussion source was needed for this local UI contract.

post_research_questions.what_changed_the_plan: Accessibility references reinforced using a hidden live region rather than fully removing status text.
post_research_questions.what_risks_remain: Only provider settings uses this pattern today.
post_research_questions.what_validation_is_required: Renderer tests, readiness, Browser layout smoke, and internal package build.
